declared: Milestone 11B closeout. Committed BEFORE any hosted judge call on the synthetic controls or the pilot. The local judge (llama3.1:8b, Q4_K_M) failed judge-validation-v1; that result is preserved and is NOT a reason to change anything here. This profile applies judge-validation-v1 to a hosted judge. It changes no threshold, no control, no expected verdict, no judge prompt (gen-judge-2) and no rubric (gen-rubric-1). It only says how the three criteria that were written around a local runtime (T3, T5, T6) identify the judge when the provider is a hosted API, and which parts of the local runtime description do not exist for a hosted API.

judge.model_rule: No model id is named here: availability cannot be verified offline and an id must not be invented. The operator names the judge model with --judge-model on every command and with --expect-judge-model on judge-validate; the report records it, and T5H fails if any artifact was judged by a different id. A model that differs from the generation model is preferred; if the same model is used the report states self-preference bias.
judge.max_output_tokens: the frozen protocol's judge.max_output_tokens (passed to judge-validate from the protocol, not chosen here)

inherited_unchanged.meaning: Same rule, same threshold, read from judge-validation-v1.json (pinned above by sha256). T2 still needs all 18 first-pass model controls to parse (0.95 of 18). S5 still needs >= 0.95 identical correctness scores between two independent passes. The controls (controls-v1.json), expected verdicts and the 8-answer pilot rules (no kappa below n = 30; fewer than 4 rated answers is inconclusive) are unchanged.

T3.rule: No successful judgement may show completion tokens plus reasoning tokens at or above the protocol's judge output cap, and token counts must be present. The input-window half of v1 T3 has no hosted counterpart (see not_applicable); a request the provider rejects for length is a failed record, as for any provider error.

T5.rule: Every controls and pilot artifact names provider gemini and exactly the model id given with --expect-judge-model, and all artifacts agree. This replaces the fingerprint, digest, quantization, seed and context checks, which a hosted API does not expose.

T6.rule: Unchanged independence checks (second pass bypasses the cache, uses its own directory, reuses nothing) plus: both passes were judged by the same provider and model id.

not_applicable.model_digest: A hosted API returns no weights digest.
not_applicable.quantization: Not controllable or reported for a hosted model.
not_applicable.context_size_input_overflow: No client-side window is configured; the hosted window is far larger than any judge prompt here. Silent input truncation is not a documented behaviour of this client's hosted path, but that is not verified; the guard against output truncation (T3) remains.
not_applicable.seed: The hosted client sets temperature 0 but no seed; hosted output is therefore NOT claimed to be deterministic, which is exactly what S5 measures.
not_applicable.structured_output_mode: The hosted judge relies on the prompt's strict-JSON instruction, not a server-side JSON mode.
not_applicable.runtime_fingerprint: No local runtime exists to fingerprint. The requested model id is the only identity this client records; a provider may re-point a model id over time, so judging must not straddle a provider-announced model change.

procedural_requirements: Do not resume a controls or pilot judge run to re-attempt items that failed with 'invalid judge output': that would mask format unreliability that T2 and T1 exist to measure. Resume only after transport interruptions (HTTP 429/503/504, timeout, circuit breaker).
Run the validation (controls, pilot, human agreement) before any primary judging, and keep validation, pilot and primary artifacts in separate directories.
Record the judge model id and the date of each run; a result is tied to that id only.
Report self-preference: whether the judge model equals the generation model (gemini-3.6-flash), and note that a different model from the same vendor reduces but does not remove it.
interpretation: Meeting T1-T6 and S1-S5 means the hosted judge showed no pilot-level red flag; it does not validate the judge. Only the primary-audit criteria P1-P4, evaluated once on the primary human audit, decide whether conclusions that depend on the judge are validated or EXPLORATORY.
